column6: CRAO - Mainstreaming Climate-Resilient Agriculture in Regional Programs and Projects (Climate Resilient Communities, Livelihoods, and Enterprises)
column8: AMIA focuses on mainstreaming climate change adaptation, beginning with the Department’s plans, programs, and budgets. Beyond the DA’s core functions, the AMIA Program also tackles regional assessment, targeting through the climate-risk vulnerability assessment (CRVA), community action for CRA, CRA capacity-building, and CRA innovations and services. Other project components deal with Participatory Climate Risk & Vulnerability Assessment (PCRVA) farmer-led participatory action research to determine the applicability of CRA options, community organizing, livelihood diversification strategies for climate-resilient value chains, enhanced access to support services (e.g. financing/ credit, insurance, post-harvest mechanization, market links) including Climate Information Services (CIS) for weather-informed farmed advisories and early warning, and systematizing evidence, monitoring and evaluation (M&E) of CRA outcomes.

column4: BFAR - Region V - Aquaculture Development Program
column8:
The development of aquaculture, focusing on freshwater, brackish water, and marine areas, is essential for increasing and enhancing productivity. This subprogram aims to identify, develop, and expand new fish/shellfish farming areas, such as offshore and inland bodies of water, for mariculture and aquaculture development, including underutilized FLA-covered areas to boost production. BFAR also identifies strategic areas nationwide for establishing community-based multi-species hatcheries. The Bureau regularly produces quality broodstock and fingerlings through its National Technology Centers and Regional/Provincial Fisheries Outreach Stations.

Key initiatives include operating nine Technology Outreach Stations as demonstration facilities for fish farmers, LGUs, and private sector partners, broodstock development, seedstock production to ensure a quality supply of breeders and fingerlings, and establishing seaweed nurseries with the distribution of seaweed propagules and farm implement

column4: BFAR - Region IX - Aquaculture Productivity Enhancement Project

column4: BFAR - CAR - Fisheries Development Program
column8:
To achieve the sectoral targets for fisheries and support the Department's goals, as well as meet the commitments in the Philippine Development Plan (PDP) 2023-2028, the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) will implement key initiatives under the National Fisheries Program, including the Fisheries Development Program. This program has four sub-programs: 

1. Capture Fisheries, which provides fiberglass boats, fishing gear, and tools to improve marine capture.
2. Aquaculture, focusing on increasing production by providing fingerlings, seaweed propagules, cages, and seaweed farming tools.
3. Post-harvest, aims to reduce post-catch losses and improve product quality through better storage, processing, and distribution systems.
4. Market Development, focused on strengthening market linkages, improving competitiveness, and enhancing supply chains.

These initiatives aim to boost fisheries productivity, enhance livelihoods, and ensure sustainable sectoral growth.

column4: FDC - Region IVA - Modernization of Integrated Laboratory Services Division
column6: FDC - Operation and Maintenance of the Integrated Laboratories
column8:
The modernization of the DA Region 4A Integrated Laboratories Division (DA Region 4A-ILD) is imperative for several compelling reasons. Firstly, it will significantly enhance productivity and efficiency in agricultural research and testing processes, allowing for the timely and accurate delivery of results to farmers and policymakers. Additionally, modernized laboratories can play a pivotal role in ensuring food safety by conducting advanced and precise testing for contaminants, pathogens, and pesticides in agricultural products, thereby safeguarding public health

 Modernizing the DA Region 4A-ILD delivers a multitude of benefits to various stakeholders. Farmers reap the advantages of precise soil and fertilizer testing, enabling them to optimize crop yields, minimize input costs, and enhance agricultural sustainability. Additionally, plant and animal disease diagnostics protect their livestock and crops, ensuring the health of agricultural practices. Agricultural enterprises benefit by gaining access to state-of-the-art testing services, which secure product quality and safety, ensuring market access and compliance with international standards. Consumers, on the other hand, enjoy improved food safety, as rigorous testing guarantees that agricultural products meet stringent quality and safety requirements, reducing health risks and ensuring confidence in the food supply.

column4: An Innovative Technique for Estimating Crop Water Requirement in Hydroponic Systems
column6: Construction of Agricultural and  Analytical Services Laboratory
column8:
The deep-water culture (DWC), in which plant roots are continuously submerged in a nutrient-rich, well-oxygenated fluid will be used in this study. The DWC is a passive type hydroponic system which ensures plants are kept hydrated, in contrast to other hydroponic systems such as the drip system and Ebb and Flow, which only water plants periodically.  
In this proposed study, a water tank equipped with a manometer will be installed to the original DWC setup to monitor water loss throughout the production period. Two tables will be used: some rows will be used for planting hydroponic crops and other rows will be left empty to serve as negative control. Through this, only water utilized by hydroponic plants is accounted for, removing any effects of evaporation, by deducting the recorded water loss from the negative control tank from the water loss recorded in the tank from the planted table. The setup will be placed within a greenhouse to reduce the possibility of confounding factors that could affect the measurement of water usage by the hydroponic crops (Figure 3). A thermometer, psychrometer, and evaporation pan will also be used and situated inside the greenhouse to account for other environmental factors and to ensure a more comprehensive data collection.

column8:
The University of Science and Technology of Southern Philippines (USTP) – Balubal Campus seeks to contribute meaningfully to the community by championing Food Security and aligning with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 2 – Zero Hunger). With its academic niche in Precision Agriculture, the campus integrates Information Technology (BSIT) for internet-based farm operations, computer applications, geomatics technologies, and data analytics, alongside Technology and Livelihood Education (BTLED) to promote community adoption of innovations.

The PEACE Program adopts the Asset-Based Community Development (ABCD) approach, encouraging grassroots participation in planning and project implementation to promote empowerment and sustainability. It prioritizes underserved communities in Cagayan de Oro and other parts of Region 10, addressing poverty (SDG 1), Zero Hunger (SDG 2), and gender equality (SDG 5).

The PEACE Program integrates agriculture, technology, and livelihood education to empower rural and peri-urban communities in Northern Mindanao through sustainable farming practices, nutrition enhancement, and community-based enterprise. It is built on three interdisciplinary components—GROW-UP, AGRI-NNOVATE, and CARE-LINK—ensuring holistic development from production to market access and social empowerment.
GROW-UP  (Green and Resilient Opportunities for Wealth through Unified Production)
Enhancing farm productivity through climate-resilient and precision-based agriculture, livestock and poultry production, and feeding systems.

AGRI-NNOVATE (Agricultural Growth and Rural Innovation through Technology and Enterprise)

Fostering agri-entrepreneurship and market-oriented innovations through technology transfer, product value-adding, and cooperative strengthening.

CARE-LINK (Community Action for Resilience, Empowerment, and Linkages for Inclusive Nutrition and Knowledge-sharing)

Strengthening community resilience, nutrition awareness, and stakeholder linkages for sustainable food security.

column4: BFAR - Region IVB - Municipal Fisherfolk Capacity Enhancement Project in Occidental Mindoro
column8:
The project entails for the procurement of three modernizing local fishing operations by procuring and distributing a new fleet - Handline Fishing Boats, upgrading traditional methods with durable, efficient assets for enhanced safety and productivity. Each vessel features a high-strength Fiber Glass Reinforced Plastic (FRP) hull, measuring a minimum 62  feet-LOA and 13GT, and includes a practical 3-ton fish hold capacity. They are powered by a reliable, brand new 170 HP, 4-stroke Diesel Marine Engine, providing the necessary capability for extended offshore operations. To ensure safety and navigation, every boat is fully equipped with modern devices, including a GPS, VHF Marine Radio, Magnetic Compass, and Echo Sounder. The construction is strategically split between shipyards in Malabon City (Pacificfortia Marine Technologies, Inc.) and Danao City, Cebu,(Dynacast Shipbuilding and Repairs Inc.)  facilitating efficient production and regional distribution. Ultimately, this significant investment will improve fisherfolk's access to deeper fishing grounds, substantially increasing their catch and economic returns while promoting safer, more sustainable fishing practices. The vessel will operate in the fishing grounds of MIMAROPA Region. 

Each commercial fishing vessel costs Php 15 million. The target is to distribute three vessels in the municipality of Mamburao, Sablayan, and San Jose in the Province of Occidental Mindoro. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  To ensure sustainable and successful operation, the initiative will empower local fisherfolk through targeted training programs focused specifically on the operation and management of these medium-scale commercial fishing vessels. This specialized training such as; 62-footer Fishing Boat Operations, Repair and Maintenance Program, Financial Literacy and Management and Training for sustainable fisheries Management, Post-harvest loss reduction, Catch Reporting, and FRP Boat Maintenance aims to enhance the skills and capacity of the associations in Occidental Mindoro, preparing them for profitable and responsible commercial fishing practices.

column4: FDC-ILD - RFO I - Completion of the Ilocos Region Integrated Agricultural Laboratory Building (IRIAL) located at Tebag, Sta. Barbara Pangasinan - Establishment of Soil and Plant Tissue Processing and Storage Building and Animal Crematorium
column6: FDC - Operation and Maintenance of the Integrated Laboratories
column8:
Strengthening and integration of laboratory services to support the implementation of the different DA banner programs, execution of mandated regulatory functions (RA 10611, RA 1556), research, development, and extension (RD & E) projects/activities focused on the current and emerging issues on agricultural production, and provision of various agricultural production support services has been the continuing tasks of DA-RFO I's Integrated Laboratories Division (ILD). 

Herein, laboratory services of the DA-RFO I's ILD are being carried out by the four (4) component laboratories of the ILD, namely Regional Animal Disease Diagnostics Laboratory (RADDL), Regional Crop Protection Center (RCPC), Regional Feed Chemical Analysis Laboratory (RFCAL), and Regional Soils Laboratory (RSL).  

Correspondingly, the DA-RFO I had started its laboratory master plan towards laboratory competency through establishment of the Ilocos Region Integrated Agricultural Laboratories (IRIAL) Complex at Tebag, Sta. Barbara, Pangasinan. Initially, the construction of the IRIAL Building, which housed the four (4) component laboratories of the DA-RFO I's ILD, and the Biocontrol Agents (BCA) Production Building has been started with an investments amounting to PhP 82,151, 726 and PhP5,000,000.00, respectively. 

However, these laboratory facilities of the DA-RFO I's ILD has not been completed, hence not fully operational. Site development and finishing works including the upgrading of the existing electrical service entrance needs to be completed. Meanwhile, other equally critical laboratory facilities intended in the IRIAL Complex, namely Animal Crematorium and Soil & Plant Tissue Sample Processing were not yet started. This proposal includes completion of newly constructed laboratory facilities and the establishment of support facilities of the IRIAL Complex for improved delivery of laboratory services on Soil Health,  Animal Diseases, and Animal Feed testing.

Multi-location nursery establishment will amplify the survival rate of quality planting materials and will enable farmers to have access to quality planting materials. Nursery producing high quality coffee planting materials is necessary to build a successful model for commercial production.
Rejuvenation and fertilization of existing coffee trees are essential practices in maintaining coffee productivity and quality. Coffee trees produce decreases as it ages due to factors like pest damage, diseases and natural wear. Rejuvenation reduces the need for replanting
